newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia noon rubber mixed, tracks Tokyo trend.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia noon rubber mixed, tracks Tokyo trend.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were mixed at midday after tracking a similar trend in Tokyo, on the absence of demand, traders said.
"It's quiet and following Tokyo," said a dealer.
A government trading source said there were no reports of sales or inquiries in Friday's early session.
Another trader said the recent weakness of Thai rubber prices was also a factor for the depressed local market.
"All overseas buyers seem sidelined at the moment," said a trader. "We haven't got anything from Middle East, China, U.S. or Europe."
At noon, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted July RSS1 buyer at 266.50 cents ($1.06) a kg, down one cent from Thursday's close. July SMR20 buyer was up half cent to 247.
Dealers offered SMR CV at 313 cents, SMR L at 292,SMR 10 at 246, SMR 20 at 245 and latex at 214.
A Malaysia-based shipping agent quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $800 per TEU and $1,700 per two-TEU containers.
